summary: Week four. 16 messages — 6 from Kaitlynn, 10 from ALTR — but the distribution is the story: every single client message landed in a six-hour burst on 2026-08-21, the first day of the window, and she has said nothing since 18:53 that evening. That is 6 days 14 hours of client silence on an account that was chatty and effusive three weeks ago. The one genuinely good thing: invoice one is paid. She confirmed it herself — 'The last invoice was paid. Had to jump through a few hoops with the wire transfer. Not sure why. The 91.00$ wasn’t included but I can send that thru Zelle or just with the next wire. 😇' — which closes last week's biggest unknown, and Derrek waived the $91 on the spot ('coupon for being such a great new client'). She took it well. Everything else got worse. No invoice has been issued for Aug 15-21 or Aug 22-28: ALTR billed once, got paid, and then stopped billing. Two full service periods are now unbilled, and her direct question 'For invoicing, is it weekly or bi-weekly typically?' is 11 days old and still unanswered by Stephski, who has not posted in the group since 2026-08-15. The Aug 19 drop of brand-new never-sold content — the one milestone she named on day one — has now been ignored for 21 days and 9 days past the date itself; the string 'aug 19' still appears exactly once in the entire chat history, in her own 2026-08-07 message. The voice-memo offer is 21 days unanswered, its fourth consecutive week. The call Mayson agreed to on 8/14 is 14 days unbooked. The posting-cadence request is 14 days unacknowledged. Then on 2026-08-27, after nine days of total group silence, ALTR broke it with three messages — and all three were demands on her, not reports to her: Ollie asked 'Hey Kaitlynn where have you been bringing subs in these last few days?' and 'From a GG swap?', and Mayson asked 'Hey Kaitlynn how come you’re not using the domain on instagram?'. That is the first reference to account performance by anyone at ALTR in 21 days and it took the form of a question. All three are still unanswered. Note what Mayson's question reveals: kaitlynn.vip, last week's headline win, has sat unused for 13 days and nobody checked until now. Note what Ollie's reveals: subs are arriving from a source ALTR does not know about. One avoidable self-inflicted wound: at 18:44 on 8/21 Derrek posted 'Kaitlynn hey! Could you clear this up when you had a chance' into the Invoicing thread — a dunning-style chase aimed at a different chat, sent six hours after she had told them she'd paid. She replied 'Did I not message about this today? I’m confused', then '??', then a photo. Derrek apologised within nine minutes and she said 'No worries 💘💘'. Recovered cleanly, but it is the only time this client has shown irritation in 21 days and ALTR caused it.

health.rationale: Down 10 from 80 (92 → 85 → 80 → 70). The decline accelerated rather than continued, and the reason is that a new failure mode opened while none of the old ones closed. Credit where due: invoice one was paid — the single largest unknown on the account last week — and Derrek's $91 waiver was handled warmly. That is worth roughly +5 on its own. It is cancelled and then some by four things. (1) Billing stopped: no invoice for Aug 15-21, none for Aug 22-28, two unbilled service periods, and the cadence question is 11 days unanswered by a Stephski who has not posted since 8/15. (2) The stale-promise stack aged another 7 days with zero movement — Aug 19 drop 21 days, voice memo 21 days, call 14 days, posting cadence 14 days, Mica Calendly 17 days. Nothing was closed. (3) The client went quiet for the first time. Her last message is 2026-08-21T18:53; three direct ALTR questions on 8/27 are unanswered. Last week's state predicted 'a client this accommodating does not escalate — she disengages'. That is now happening on schedule. (4) ALTR's only substantive outbound this week was three extraction questions after nine days of silence — still, at 21 days into the account, not one unprompted performance update has ever been posted in this chat. Not lower than 70 because she paid, she is not angry, there is still no formal complaint, and the relationship is recoverable this week with two phone calls and one invoice.
